 Fort Bend County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0020
 Sara Davis, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
October 11, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Debra Moody, Brown & Shaw Law Group
PARTIES
Plaintiff Sara Davis is an individual residing in Texas who was injured in the collision described below. Defendant is an
automobile insurance carrier authorized to do business in the State of Texas, which issued the policy under which Plaintiff seeks
coverage and benefits.
FACTS
On June 4, 2023, Plaintiff was lawfully operating a passenger vehicle on a public roadway in Sugar Land, Texas. Plaintiff was
turning left at an intersection when another motorist, traveling in the opposite direction, struck Plaintiff's vehicle. The impact
caused Plaintiff's vehicle to strike the roadway and sustained damage to its front and driver-side areas. Plaintiff reported the
collision promptly and submitted a claim under the applicable coverage, including medical payments and uninsured or
underinsured motorist benefits where applicable. Defendant has not paid the claim in full and has not provided a written
explanation of its position within the time required by Texas law.
NEGLIGENCE
The at-fault driver failed to yield the right of way, failed to keep a proper lookout, and failed to take reasonable action to avoid
the collision. Those failures constitute negligence. Defendant is liable under the policy terms and under Texas law for benefits
owed to Plaintiff, and Defendant breached its contractual obligations by delaying and underpaying the claim without a reasonable
basis.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered a concussion, with headaches, dizziness, light sensitivity, and cognitive
difficulty. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses for emergency care, imaging, and ongoing treatment, lost wages from missed
work, and suffered physical pain, metnal anguish, and diminished enjoyment of life. These losses are expected to continue.
Plaintiff seeks damages in the amount of $233,000.00, together with statutory interest, attorney's fees, and court costs as allowed
under Texas law.
